observations.limitations: The sentence is metaphorical, although “makanan enak” plainly concerns food quality.
observations.observation: A comparison involving a chef describes appealing food as “makanan enak.”
observations.source_title: Sokongan Minim APBD Bukan Masalah, Bupati Sugiri Jamin Kualitas Grebeg Suro Tetap Terjaga

observations.limitations: Natural use is visible; relative frequency against “sedap” was not measured.
observations.observation: The article contrasts food that “rasanya enak” or “makanan enak” with healthy food, using “enak” without explanation.

observations.limitations: The entry also records smell and non-food senses.
observations.observation: The entries define a taste sense equivalent to “enak” and illustrate it with “kuih.”

observations.limitations: The same page also calls food and dishes “enak” at lines 53 and 65–67, so it does not establish that “sedap” is the sole or invariably preferred choice.
observations.observation: The page headlines its food selection “Makanan yang sedap.”

observations.limitations: This confirms a live alternative but does not quantify whether it is as common as “sedap.”
observations.observation: The same Malaysian food page uses “enak” for dishes and local food.

observations.limitations: The observations support natural choices, but “normal” as a frequency ranking remains unmeasured.
observations.observation: Indonesian public guidance naturally uses “enak” for food taste; a Malaysian food page uses “sedap” prominently, while also using “enak.”
observations.publisher: Kementerian Kesehatan Republik Indonesia; Penang Hill Corporation
